metadata.notes: Path A — Direct Prompt Injection. Scenario: LegitimateAgentCompromised (Layer 2 AI-Specific). Attacker manipulates agent through its designed input interface (first #1). Agent abuses its own tool-use capabilities (second #1) to exfiltrate data or modify systems. Both steps exploit functional scope, not implementation flaws. Notation: #1→[instant]#1 + [DRE: C, I]. Velocity: VC-4 — entire chain executes within single inference cycle. No human-speed gaps. Only architectural controls (capability restriction, output filtering) are viable. Source: 'Agentic AI Under the Microscope — Why AI Security Is Not a Threat Category' (Bernhard Kreinz, 2026-02-25).

path_sequence.notes: Direct prompt injection via designed natural language interface. Generic vulnerability: scope, complexity, and inherent trust in agent's instruction-processing capability. No implementation flaw required — the LLM's instruction-following across its context window is the designed capability being abused.
Agent abuses tool-use capabilities (API calls, data access, file operations) per injected instructions. Generic vulnerability: scope and trust placed in agent's designed tool-use functions.
